daily_basics: Water, then soup, then plate. Eat slowly.
Walk every day. Start with 10 minutes.
Muscle exercise 2 days a week (push-ups, squats)
No snacking on fried food at work
Eat breakfast and dinner too. Same rules.
safety_notes: Not zero fat: your body needs a little. Too much food makes body fat.
Diabetes, kidney or heart problems, high blood pressure, pregnant, breastfeeding, under 18, or on medicine? Ask your doctor first.
Lose slowly: at most 1 kg (2 lb) a week. Eat 3 meals; never starve.
Chest pain or very dizzy? Stop and get help now.
Allergy? Tell the kitchen. Always worried about food? Talk to a doctor. Help is normal.
assumptions: Nutrition numbers are estimates, not lab tests. Jalsa publishes no nutrition data, so they come from the research ranges (USDA FoodData Central, IFCT 2017 / INDB, CoFID and lab-tested UK and Irish takeaway data). Real dishes can vary 2-3 times in oil, ghee and cream.

Method: each est_* range is the sum of its parts (main + side + carb + drink), each scaled by the share eaten, rounded outward (kcal to 10, grams to 1). A request that only cuts fat lowers the upper bound only, scaled to the share eaten: no butter on a tandoor plate -5 g fat / -45 kcal; less oil or light tadka on a curry or dal -10 g fat / -90 kcal; little dosa oil -5 g fat. A request that takes a part off the plate lowers both ends: no rice (roti days), roti wrap instead of paratha (-8 g fat, -70 kcal; no mayo -5 g fat on the upper end only), one spoon of coconut chutney (about -3.5 to -11 g fat), no chutney on Day 21 (-6 to -15 g fat).

Targets check (middle of each range): every day is inside 450-650 kcal (Days 3 and 17 lowest at about 490, Days 2 and 15 highest at about 645), 6 g saturated fat or less, 25 g protein or more (lowest about 27 g on Days 21 and 30) and 8 g fibre or more (lowest about 8 g on Days 3, 12, 17, 22). Fat is 22 g or less on every non-salmon day (highest about 21.6 g on the Chicken Jalfrezi days); salmon days are about 23-24 g, mostly unsaturated fish fat. Plan-wide middles: about 596 kcal, 18 g fat, 3.9 g saturated fat, 40 g protein and 13 g fibre.

The high end of 28 of 30 days is above 650 kcal (all but Days 3 and 17), and salmon days with spinach soup can reach about 9 g saturated fat. Lunches will be bigger if the kitchen uses more oil or bigger portions; that is why every day has a kitchen request. Saturated fat and fibre were estimated per day for checking only and are not printed.

Portions: soup bowl 300-350 ml; 'small bowl' = about 2/3 of a bowl (about 1 cup). Tandoor plates hold 170-250 g cooked protein: 'eat ¾' = about 130-190 g, 'eat ½' = about 85-125 g. Curry entree about 375 g: 'eat pieces, leave gravy' is counted as ¾ of the entree (conservative, since most oil is in the gravy); Mix Daal ¾ bowl, Chana Masala ½ bowl, Yellow Daal a full bowl with light tadka. Leftovers go home for dinner and are not counted in lunch.
Days 9 and 19 eat only half the tandoor chicken because they have a full bowl of Lentil Soup plus half rice; this keeps the fibre at about 10 g and the middle under 650 kcal, with about 46 g protein.

The rice that comes with tandoor and curry plates is assumed to be plain white rice (160-250 g), so 'half the rice on your plate' = about 80-125 g. The data uses the menu name 'Vegan Steamed White Rice' only because it is the plain rice on the menu; the printed portion text tells the reader not to order an extra rice side. If the kitchen serves yellow rice, ask for plain (yellow rice adds about 5-12 g fat).

One carb only: on roti days the plate's rice is skipped ('no rice'), not added to. Tandoori Roti is marked vegan (V) on the menu, so it should come with no butter or ghee; ask whether it is 100% whole wheat (atta). On idly, dosa and kathi-roll days the idly, dosa or wrap is the carb, so carb = 'none'.

Idly and dosa plates come with about 1 cup of sambar and 40-60 g of coconut chutney; 'one spoon' = about 15 g. Coconut chutney is the main saturated-fat source on these plates. '3 idly' is the top of the 2-3 idly plate in the research.

Kathi rolls (Days 7 and 28) assume the kitchen can wrap them in a tandoori roti instead of a paratha, with no mayo. If not, eat Tandoori Chicken Tikka with 1 roti (Day 7) or any green dish (Day 28), as the day's 'why' says. If the stiff roti cracks, eat the filling with the roti.

The menu does not describe Tandoori Ghost Chicken; it is assumed to be boneless ghost-pepper chicken tikka (if it is too hot, choose Tandoori Chicken Tikka). Tandoori Chicken Leg is assumed to be 2 skinless leg quarters; the plan eats one and takes the rest home.

Drinks: water by default. Masala chai with no sugar and a little milk = about 40-70 kcal and 1-3 g fat; it is on the idly Days 5 and 23 only. If the kitchen's chai is already sweet, drink water. Soda Shikanji was removed from the plan (salty, often pre-sweetened).

Spinach Soup is on Days 1, 6, 16, 20 and 25, about once a week, so leafy-green intake stays even (relevant for people on warfarin). Its recipe is unknown; a coconut-milk finish would raise saturated fat, hence 'ask: no coconut milk'.

Lamb and goat are left out of the 30 days: even with kitchen changes, the estimated lamb and goat lunches go over the fat and saturated-fat targets. The menu has no pork. The plan assumes the person eats chicken, fish and shrimp; 17 of the 30 days are vegetarian, fish or shrimp.
Free-choice days (7, 14, 21, 28) show a suggested dish. Any green dish, or a yellow dish ordered with its kitchen request, can replace it. These are planned flexible days, not cheat days.

Age, sex, weight, height, activity, health and religion are unknown, so this is general adult guidance, not medical advice. Without a doctor, women should not eat less than about 1,200 kcal a day and men about 1,500 (AHA/ACC/TOS); the printed note says 'Eat 3 meals; never starve' because the reader does not count calories. People with kidney disease should not follow the high-protein tandoor days without advice. Over 65, gallstones before, or an eating disorder now or in the past: get advice first. A yearly check of blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol is a good idea (South Asian adults have higher risk at lower weights).

Allergy swaps (not printed for space): shellfish allergy, eat Chicken Jalfrezi on shrimp days; fish allergy, eat Tandoori Chicken Tikka on salmon days; wheat or gluten, take half rice instead of roti and skip the kathi rolls; milk, note that tandoori marinades use yogurt and chai has milk; nuts, ask what is in the chana and jalfrezi sauces.

Sodium was not estimated per dish. As a rough guide, a restaurant soup plus a curry or salted tandoor marinade plus roti or sambar is likely about 1,200-2,500 mg sodium (3-6 g salt) per lunch, against the WHO limit of under 2,000 mg a day. So every kitchen request says 'less salt', golden rule 5 says no pickle, and soups are small bowls except Days 9, 11, 14 and 19 (a full Lentil Soup for fibre or protein).

Traffic light: green = fits the lunch targets with the kitchen request; yellow = only sometimes, or only with a change; red = rare treat, about once a month: share it or eat half (fried, creamy, buttery, ghee, paneer, coconut milk, lamb or goat, biryani, naan or paratha, sugary or salty drinks, desserts). None of the 30 lunches uses a red item.

Not applied (nutrition audit, 'Ask less salt. No pickle, no papad.' as a daily basic): salt became golden rule 5 and is in all 30 kitchen requests, so the 5 daily basics are kept for meal order, walking, muscle work, snacking and 3 meals.

Not applied (nutrition audit, 'Small chana' side on Days 9/19; safety audit, 'Small cup of chana'): the chana side was removed, as the menu-fit audit asked, because Chana Masala is a full entree with its own rice.

Not applied (menu-fit audit, Spinach or Veggie Soup on Days 9/19 and Veggie Soup on Days 7/14): with Spinach or Veggie Soup these days fall to about 5-8 g fibre, under the 8 g target, so they keep Lentil Soup; Days 9 and 19 eat half the chicken to stay under 650 kcal.
Not applied (menu-fit audit, Spinach Soup on Days 3 and 17): Veggie Soup is used, because spinach soup (possibly coconut-milk finished) pushed these shrimp days to the fat and saturated-fat limits.

Not applied (menu-fit audit, 'Never eat under 1,200 calories a day' printed): one number does not fit both sexes and the reader does not count calories, so the note says 'Eat 3 meals; never starve' and the 1,200 / 1,500 kcal floors are kept in these assumptions.
Not applied (menu-fit audit, 'Extra sambar' on idly days): protein already meets 25 g with a small Lentil Soup, and extra sambar adds salt and up to about 120 kcal.

Not applied (safety audit, a 7th golden rule for salt): the limit is 6 rules, so salt replaced 'Soup first, then eat slowly' as rule 5, and that habit moved to daily basics ('Water, then soup, then plate. Eat slowly.').
Not applied (safety audit, small soup bowls on every day): Days 9, 11, 14 and 19 keep a full bowl of Lentil Soup, needed for fibre (Days 9, 14, 19) or protein (Day 11).

Not applied (safety audit, full allergy swaps and the full list of doctor groups in the printed notes): the 4-note, 16-word limit leaves room only for 'Allergy? Tell the kitchen' and the main groups; the swaps, over 65, gallstones and the yearly checks are listed in these assumptions. 'High blood pressure? Always ask less salt' is covered by golden rule 5 and the doctor note instead of its own note.

Not applied (safety audit, 'extra salad' in tandoor-day requests and Panch Ratan Sabzi as a Day 26 side): the 6-word request has no room after the fat, salt and carb asks, salad is not a menu item, and the sabzi is a full entree with its own rice (two entrees). Tandoor days still reach about 10 g fibre from roti and soup. The plate formula stays 'Protein + soup + ...' because every lunch has a soup.

Not applied (safety audit, Ghost Chicken request 'Ask what is in it. Skin off...'): too long for 6 words, and the person works in this kitchen; Day 4 says 'Too hot? Choose chicken tikka.' 'Skin off' was also dropped on the Chicken Leg day, since tandoori chicken is skinned before marinating (menu-fit audit).

Not applied (safety audit, Desi Chinese dishes added to red): they are not in menu.json and may come from an old sheet seen through the paper, and the traffic light must hold exactly the 123 menu items. A renderer line could say: 'Not on this list? Fried, creamy, buttery or sweet = rare treat.'

Not applied here (safety audit, renderer changes): dropping 'g fat' from the day cards, rounding kcal to 50, and the tracker note about plateaus belong in render.cjs, not in the plan data. Suggested tracker text: 'Slow is good. Weight goes down, then stops for a while. This is normal. Keep going!'

Not applied (safety audit, 'Water or seltzer with lemon' on Days 7 and 24; nutrition audit, 'Plain roti wrap, no mayo'): the drink is simply 'Water' (seltzer is fine too: Soda Can is yellow as 'Seltzer water only'), and the roll request uses 'less salt' instead of 'plain', because the menu marks Tandoori Roti vegan (no butter).

PDF readability review (reader + phone/print lenses) applied: clearer portion wording (fractions in words, 'eat the chicken, not the gravy', rice 'half portion (ask the kitchen)'), explained 'Your choice' days, Masala Chai (no sugar) moved to green, Soda Can limited to plain sparkling water, split urgent vs gentle safety notes. No nutrition choices changed.
